source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00EC (lemma-idempotent-spec: Spec R = D(e) ⊔ D(1-e), the image of an idempotent in a residue field is 0 or 1) and Lemma 00ED (lemma-spec-product)

proof.text: Clause 2. In the Zariski topology of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] every principal open $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ is open, so by step 2 every singleton $\{\mathfrak p_j\}=D(e_j)$ is open. Every subset of $\operatorname{Spec}C=\{\mathfrak p_1,\dots,\mathfrak p_n\}$ is the union of its singletons, hence open: the topology is discrete.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00EC (D(e) open, with complement D(1-e))

proof.text: $\pi_j$ is a localization of $C$ at $e_j$. Regard $L_j$ as a $C$-algebra via $\pi_j$. We check the characterization of a localization at one element in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]: (a) $\pi_j(e_j)=1$ is a unit of $L_j$; (b) every element $x\in L_j$ is $\pi_j(c)\cdot\pi_j(e_j)^{-0}$ for $c=(0,\dots,x,\dots,0)$, since $\pi_j$ is surjective; (c) $\pi_j(c)=0\iff c_j=0\iff ce_j=0$ (step 1), and $e_j^kc=e_jc$ for $k\ge1$, so $\pi_j(c)=0$ iff $e_j^kc=0$ for some $k\ge0$ (for $k=0$, $c=0$ gives $\pi_j(c)=0$ too). Hence the induced map $C_{e_j}\to L_j$, $c/e_j^m\mapsto\pi_j(c)$, is an isomorphism of $C$-algebras, i.e. $\pi_j$ factors as $C\to C_{e_j}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }L_j$. This is the claim $R_1=R_{e_1}$ that Stacks leaves to the reader in the proof of Lemma 00ED.

proof.text: Clause 3. By step 4, $\pi_j=\beta\circ\lambda$ with $\lambda:C\to C_{e_j}$ the localization map and $\beta:C_{e_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_j$ a ring isomorphism. By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}\pi_j=\operatorname{Spec}\lambda\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta$, where $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ is an isomorphism of schemes and $\operatorname{Spec}\lambda:\operatorname{Spec}C_{e_j}\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an open immersion with image the principal open $D(e_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. An isomorphism followed by an open immersion is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] (it is still a homeomorphism onto the same open subset, and the sheaf map $(\operatorname{Spec}\pi_j)^{-1}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}L_j}$ is the composite of two isomorphisms), with the same image $D(e_j)=\{\mathfrak p_j\}$ (step 2). (Directly: the single point $(0)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}L_j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] maps to $\pi_j^{-1}(0)=\mathfrak p_j$.) Hence $\operatorname{Spec}\pi_j$ induces an isomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}L_j$ onto the open subscheme $\{\mathfrak p_j\}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ (open by clause 2).

lean.statement: theorem spec_finite_product_fields (n : ℕ) (L : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (L i)] : (∀ (p : Ideal (∀ i, L i)), p.IsPrime ↔ ∃ i : Fin n, p = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥ ≠ Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L j) ⊥) ∧ Nat.card (PrimeSpectrum (∀ i, L i)) = n ∧ DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum (∀ i, L i)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, IsOpenImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i))) ∧ Set.range (fun x : PrimeSpectrum (L i) ↦ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i))).base x) = {p | p.asIdeal = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥} ∧ ∃ U : (Spec (.of (∀ i, L i))).Opens, (U : Set (Spec (.of (∀ i, L i)))) = {p | p.asIdeal = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥} ∧ ∃ e : Spec (.of (L i)) ≅ U.toScheme, e.hom ≫ U.ι = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i)))
